papers.title: The one-step surface-air lag in the EnergyPlus zone heat balance: order of accuracy, correction and consequences
papers.abstract: The order of accuracy sets how fast numerical error falls as the timestep shortens. This study measured that order for the zone heat balance of EnergyPlus 26.2 against exact or converged references and tested a correction on 45 U.S. Department of Energy prototype cases. All three zone air formulas, the third-order default included, give first order or lower, because the surfaces use the previous timestep's air temperature. Solving surfaces, air and HVAC to agreement within each timestep raises the default to about second order, and in a room with an exact solution two extra passes cut the error eightfold at 1.65 times the runtime. In the prototype cases, the correction changed annual site energy by at most 0.45% but an outpatient clinic's heating by 5.1%. Window-upgrade savings changed by 10% or more in 13 of the 34 applicable cases, about as often as under a change of timestep.

papers.title: Approximate Recall, Approximate Forecasts: Recall as a Diagnostic for LLM Forecasting Errors
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit approximate recall: they retain coarse associations about past events while losing fidelity on specific details. Past research on LLMs has quantified different models' forecasting ability in real-world events using prediction markets, but has not studied how losing said fidelity impacts their forecasting abilities. For example: while an LLM correctly recalls that the answer to: ''Did Anna Sawai win the Best Drama Actress in the 76th Emmy Awards?'' is ''Yes,'' it incorrectly states the event date as September 22 rather than September 15. In this paper, we introduce a novel metric called the Recall Fidelity Score to study how imprecision in internalized knowledge propagates to forecasting capability on future events. On resolved historical markets, we find that higher local recall fidelity around semantically similar past events predicts lower forecasting error on resolved markets, and the same signal predicts smaller distance from open markets prices.

papers.title: TALK: One-Shot Batch Design for Protein Variant Effect Prediction
papers.abstract: Protein variant effect prediction is central to understanding protein function and guiding protein engineering, yet experimental labels remain costly. In many protein experiments, the variants that can be assayed are dictated by protocol constraints, while the variants that need accurate prediction may lie in a different or broader region of the landscape. This assay-prediction mismatch makes candidate-local criteria such as predicted function, uncertainty, or exploration value insufficient for measurement design. Given a protocol-defined accessible space and a limited budget, we ask which variants should be assayed so that the resulting data best improves landscape prediction. We propose TALK, which estimates each candidate's contribution through posterior coupling between accessible and target variants and reduces redundant information within the batch. Across retrospective ProteinGym and FLIP protocols, TALK generally improves target-space prediction under limited measurement budgets. These results point to a practical two-stage workflow: first, spend a limited assay budget on variants selected to be informative for the target landscape and train a predictive model from the measured labels; then use this model to score and prioritize high-potential variants. Code is available at https://github.com/joehuang618/TALK.

papers.title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories
papers.abstract: Large language models and the multi-agent systems built around them could accelerate materials discovery by connecting scientific knowledge with experimental decisions. Existing benchmarks establish capabilities in domain knowledge, multimodal interpretation and scientific tool use. As language models increasingly support materials research workflows, their ability to distinguish closely related material states and reason accurately with quantitative evidence remains insufficiently evaluated. These abilities are essential for comparing material responses, assessing mechanisms and maintaining reliable judgements as experimental evidence accumulates. We introduce MatScope to evaluate three connected capabilities. M1 tests unaided, condition-specific reasoning through 200 tasks spanning ten research functions, using aluminium and high-entropy alloys as representative material systems. M2 tests agent-assisted transfer of related knowledge to unresolved materials questions. MatEvoBench-20 tests initial forecasts across scientific dependency chains and revisions of still-hidden responses as observations accumulate. Across eleven model deployments, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, given-input calculations and many physical explanations are handled well. Fine-grained response estimates, comparisons between similar states and quantitatively supported choices remain substantially weaker. Related literature improves selected estimates, while condition and baseline mismatches limit transfer. Progressive observations calibrate some downstream responses and destabilize earlier accurate predictions. MatScope establishes measurable targets for developing reliable scientific reasoning in future self-evolving materials laboratories and materials-aware world models.

papers.title: An open source Python code for three-dimensional topology optimization in single precision on a consumer GPU
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional topology optimization solves linear systems with millions of unknowns at every design iteration. Consumer graphics cards run far faster in single than in double precision, and open codes for them mostly address minimum compliance. This educational article presents TOF3D, an open source Python code for density-based topology optimization in single precision on one consumer GPU. It solves four classes of problems: stress constrained minimum compliance, robust minimum compliance against manufacturing errors, compliant mechanisms and bone-like porous infill. The stiffness operator is applied without assembly, and the conjugate gradient method is preconditioned by geometric multigrid. Rounding the element matrix to single precision gave rigid body motions a spurious energy and changed compliances by up to 5.4%. Forming the element products from differences of nodal displacements reduced this error to $1.3\times 10^{-5}$ at no cost in time. Adjoint sensitivities agreed with finite differences to within $1.7\times 10^{-6}$, and the solutions agreed with Ansys Mechanical APDL to within $4.1\times 10^{-10}$ with the same element. On an RTX 3060 with 12 GB, one design iteration of a cantilever took 0.46 s with 0.5 million elements and 15 s with 33.5 million. On the same card and problem, an open GPU code that applies its operator in double precision took 3.7 and 21 s with 0.5 and 4.2 million elements and ran out of memory on larger meshes. Eight cases fixed in a protocol before the runs took 9 to 35 minutes each with 4.2 to 5.2 million elements.

papers.title: Computational Structure of Pairwise Housing Connectedness Networks
papers.abstract: Directed housing-submarket networks combine common market movement with heterogeneous bilateral relations, and different node-level measures need not yield distinct empirical rankings. We construct a positive pairwise net-connectedness network from the generalized forecast error variance decomposition (GFEVD) of a vector autoregression (VAR) and use it to compare complementary node positions. Net directional connectedness (NET), PageRank, and Viral Centrality summarize net directional balance, recursively weighted incoming position, and normalized multistep reach. When bilateral net differences are nonzero, the network is a weighted tournament. A least-squares edge-flow decomposition separates the pairwise-net matrix into a NET-equivalent gradient component and a NET-orthogonal residual, while a monotone-allocation condition establishes exact PageRank-indegree correspondence in a transitive tournament. In Seoul's 25-district network, the gradient component accounts for 70.9% of the squared Frobenius norm, leaving 29.1% in the residual component. PageRank is strongly aligned with indegree (Spearman $\rho=0.987$), and Viral Centrality with outdegree ($\rho=0.935$); the PageRank alignment exceeds the range of independently weighted simulations with comparable tournament consistency and edge-weight variation. Three common-component treatments reduce total connectedness from 81.98% to 50.60-52.00%, a 36.6-38.3% reduction relative to the raw system, and reverse 97-98 of 300 pairwise net directions. Thus, both the magnitude and the apparent direction of connectedness depend materially on the treatment of citywide common movement. Songpa's positive NET position remains prominent across common-component treatments and dynamic specifications and ranks first in both chronological subsamples.

papers.title: SimpFlow: Transferable Pretraining for Fluid Dynamics via Simplified Physics
papers.abstract: Neural surrogates enable rapid fluid simulation, but learning across diverse three-dimensional (3D) geometries requires costly computational fluid dynamics (CFD) labels. We introduce SimpFlow, a pretraining approach that generates supervision from simplified physics on unlabeled geometry libraries. A source-panel potential-flow solver generates velocity and pressure fields for approximately 9,000 3D geometries, capturing geometry-induced acceleration, stagnation, and suction while omitting viscosity and separated wakes. The solver imports only a surface mesh and reuses precomputed velocity fields across inflow directions, enabling inexpensive label generation. In our benchmark, amortized labeling takes 0.111 s per example using four CPU threads. We pretrain a neural surrogate on these labels and fine-tune it on independent CFD datasets. Across five flow tasks, SimpFlow improves over training from scratch in all 24 task-budget settings. With fine-tuning fixed at 200 epochs, interpolation indicates that SimpFlow requires 35-68% fewer CFD training cases to match the error of scratch models trained at each task's largest data budget. These results demonstrate that simplified physical solutions can provide transferable supervision, offering a practical way to reduce the high-fidelity data requirements of fluid surrogates.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Sinusoidal Representation Networks for Damage Identification in Ultrasonic Guided Wave Structural Health Monitoring
papers.abstract: Ultrasonic guided wave (UGW) inspection has become an effective method in structural health monitoring (SHM). While machine learning has enhanced damage detection capabilities, purely data-driven models remain constrained by extensive labeled datasets and limited physical interpretability. Standard multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) further suffer from spectral bias (F-Principle) in high-frequency regimes, prioritizing low-frequency components while failing to resolve the high-frequency oscillations critical for UGW reconstruction. Physics-Informed Sinusoidal Representation Networks (PI-SIRENs) address these limitations by embedding governing partial differential equations directly into the training process. Building upon SIRENs, which utilize periodic activation functions to inherently capture high-frequency spectral content, the proposed framework is designed to operate effectively in sparse ultrasonic measurement regimes. This work introduces a frequency-domain PI-SIREN framework tailored for the Mindlin-Reissner plate theory to reconstruct ultrasonic wavefields without temporal discretization. The model parameters are optimized using a hybrid strategy comprising three phases: first-order Adam, residual-adaptive refinement (RAR) and quasi-Newton L-BFGS. Numerical and experimental evaluations confirm that the model serves as a physics-consistent baseline derived from sparse data, functioning as a computationally efficient surrogate for damage identification in SHM and non-destructive testing (NDT). Integrating the surrogate into a damage identification pipeline detects and localizes a milled notch from sparse experimental measurements with a localization error of 1 % of the plate diagonal. In contrast, data-driven benchmarks and MLPs with hyperbolic tangent activation functions, with and without Fourier feature embedding, are unable to identify damage due to higher reconstruction errors.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks in the small-data regime: A controlled comparison with classical PDE surrogates
papers.abstract: Neural surrogates for engineering models are often trained on large collections of simulated solutions. We investigate whether physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can achieve accurate predictions from scarce labelled observations by incorporating governing equations and prescribed initial and boundary conditions. We introduce hierarchical loss weighting (H-PINN) and its gradient-direction-aware extension (HO-PINN), which adjust the emphasis on physical constraints according to higher-priority losses. Hierarchical PINNs are compared with Vanilla PINN, tuned gradient boosting, support-vector regression, and Gaussian-process regression on a heat equation and three heterogeneous two-phase-flow benchmarks. Experiments use 20--1000 labelled states and ten paired seeds. Each label is one coordinate--state observation, not a complete simulation. At least one PINN variant achieves the highest mean primary-target \(R^2\) in each interpolation and equation-assisted forecasting comparison at 20 and 50 labels. The advantage for water saturation persists across all tested budgets. Hierarchical weighting reduces variability across runs in selected settings. These results demonstrate that known physics can support accurate neural surrogate predictions from very few solution observations, at substantially higher fitting cost than the tested classical regressors.

papers.title: Input and Horizon Dependent Structural Fidelity in Chunk Coupled Spiking Networks
papers.abstract: A fixed structural edit can preserve a spike sequence under one input and change it under another. We study this dependence using statistics-preserving edge swaps, controlled inputs and finite-horizon parameter certificates. The original 125-chunk numerical model is tested on ten artificial graphs from three connection rules. Despite identical total external drive at every slot, global and focal inputs change the visibility of 4--13 of nineteen fixed swaps per graph. A paired homogeneous and heterogeneous leaky integrate-and-fire validation in brian2-atlas reuses three originals and extends observation from 30 to 300 ms under a constant background drive sufficient for isolated-cell firing. Heterogeneous short-window switching persists, but by 300 ms every tested swap differs from its reference, saturating the binary visibility readout. Fixed-support weight families provide a complementary regional guarantee. Positive certified intervals cover 4,308 of 4,320 LIF direction conditions and include distinct floating-point configurations. A post hoc comparison finds a long-window failure inside the short-window certified interval in 710 of 720 heterogeneous conditions; 394 of 829 direction pairs ordered under both matched-drive inputs change order at 300 ms. Input-specific filtering and threshold-margin scores retain useful ordering but degrade with horizon and do not consistently beat activity controls. Earlier temporal-error, paired-dose and unsuccessful structural-selection results delimit what these findings imply. Together, the evidence links input-conditioned structural effects to finite-horizon fidelity regions in two deterministic kernels, without establishing universal topology rankings, model compression or asymptotic robustness.

papers.title: Worst-Case Contagion in Financial Networks: MILP Clearing and Robust Loss Analysis
papers.abstract: We study worst-case contagion losses in financial networks with interbank liabilities and common exposures to marketable assets. Existing linear-programming approaches provide exact stress-test values only within an insolvency-resilience margin, where all institutions remain solvent with respect to the external sector. We show that this margin is computed exactly by a finite family of linear programs, one per vertex of the uncertainty ball, whereas a single linear program based on the componentwise worst deterioration of external resources yields only a certified lower bound. We extend this framework beyond that margin in three directions. First, we derive an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the maximal clearing vector under arbitrary signed external net positions, providing a clearing oracle for robust stress testing when insolvency can occur. Second, we develop certified bounds on the worst-case loss beyond the margin, including insolvency-pattern enumeration, scenario lower bounds, fixed-pattern dual upper bounds, localized certificates, and a regime-generation procedure with monotone gap certificates. Third, we analyze the worst-case loss curve as a function of the perturbation radius. For $\ell_1$ and $\ell_\infty$ price-perturbation sets, the curve is convex, nondecreasing and piecewise linear up to the margin, with breakpoints generated by switches in worst-case shock directions, LP bases, and bank-level activity patterns. Beyond the margin, it remains nondecreasing and piecewise affine, but convexity may fail, the curve may jump upward, and the worst case need not be attained. The framework provides a certifiable MILP/LP methodology for parametric stress testing and interpretable diagnostics identifying the banks responsible for changes in systemic loss.

papers.title: Regularity in Cryptocurrency Market Cycles: A Halving-to-Halving Analysis Using Data from Google Trends and Wikipedia
papers.abstract: Bitcoin halvings provide a natural temporal structure for studying long-term dynamics of cryptocurrency markets. This paper presents a methodological framework for analyzing the regularity of Bitcoin and aggregate cryptocurrency market cycles by normalizing historical periods between consecutive halving events and projecting them onto a common relative-time scale expressed as the percentage of cycle completion. The proposed framework integrates market variables, namely Bitcoin price and aggregate cryptocurrency market capitalization, with measures of public attention derived from Google Trends search volume and Wikipedia pageviews. To obtain long-horizon daily attention indices, Google Trends data are reconstructed from overlapping 90-day windows linked by median scale ratios, following established approaches to combining high-frequency Google Trends samples. Rather than attempting to forecast future prices, the study aims to compare historical cycles, identify recurring temporal patterns, and evaluate the relationship between market dynamics and retail investor interest across different cycle-relative stages. Exploratory results point to a possible recurring structure. The maxima of the aggregate market capitalization in the two most recent completed cycles occurred at 39.0% and 37.9% of cycle completion, and the highest value of the ongoing cycle observed to date at 38.1% (534-547 days after the respective halvings), although the corresponding multiple of the halving-day value fell from 66 to 1.8. Public attention shows a similar compression of peak multiples, but not a similar timing. The paper also discusses current data limitations and outlines future research directions, including formal lead-lag analyses and expanded multi-asset investigations.

papers.title: Cable construction effects on the lateral forces and wakes of helically stranded cables under oblique inflow
papers.abstract: Helically stranded cables in aerial towing systems experience oblique inflow, but are often modeled as smooth cylinders, neglecting three-dimensional cross-stream coupling and surface texture. We perform large-eddy simulations and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition for a smooth cylinder and four stranded cables at four inclinations from $22.5^\circ$ to $90^\circ$, all stationary, with $Re \approx 1.0 \times 10^4$. Aerodynamic differences are governed mainly by cross-sectional symmetry and strand-scale groove depth. Force-source decomposition shows that surface pressure contributes 94.9%--98.3% of the mean normal force and dominates the mean lateral force. High-symmetry, quasi-circular envelopes maintain balanced circumferential pressure, whereas deep-grooved, low-symmetry tri-lobed geometries produce asymmetric separation and a persistent lateral pressure imbalance. In the wake, high-symmetry cables sustain spanwise-synchronized Karman shedding at moderate-to-high inclinations, concentrating fluctuation energy in a dominant low-rank mode. Deep grooves disrupt shedding coherence, deflect the recirculation zone laterally, and spread energy across broadband scales. Mean lateral force and lateral-force fluctuations are therefore decoupled: the quasi-circular $(1 \times 19)$ cable has minimal mean lateral force but strong periodic fluctuations, while the deep-grooved $(3 \times 7)$ cable has weak fluctuations but appreciable mean lateral force. These results support construction-dependent cable selection and aerodynamic load modeling.

papers.title: Hydrograd v2.0: a differentiable two-dimensional shallow-water model on unstructured meshes with steady and unsteady adjoints for calibration and closure learning
papers.abstract: We present \textit{Hydrograd} v2.0, a significantly improved differentiable 2D shallow-water model written in Python with JAX. The model solves the shallow-water equations on the unstructured meshes of production models such as SRH-2D and HEC-RAS 2D with a well-balanced, positivity-preserving finite-volume scheme that handles wetting and drying. Gradients are tailored to the type of problem. Steady states are found by Newton's method with an exact sparse Jacobian obtained by graph colouring, and their gradients follow from the implicit function theorem at the cost of one linear solve. Unsteady flows are differentiated in reverse mode with checkpointing, or with an implicit time integrator whose gradient costs about two forward runs. All gradients agree with finite differences, to about $10^{-8}$ for steady flows. On the Savannah River case, the steady water surface differs from that of SRH-2D by 4.7\,mm (root mean square). Steady closure learning was 96 times faster than differentiating through time marching and reached a lower loss. An inflow hydrograph was inverted from stage records with a peak error of 2\,\%. In an unsteady roughness calibration, a singular value decomposition analysis of the sensitivity matrix showed that the stage records at the gauges are 70 to 160 times more sensitive to the total resistance of the reach than to its distribution among the roughness zones, which explains why only a gauge layout with gauges in every zone recovered all five roughness values. On one GPU, a mesh of 512,000 cells takes 7.6\,s for a forward run and 51\,s for a gradient.

papers.title: Law-Invariant Operators for Stochastic Mechanics
papers.abstract: A central objective in stochastic mechanics is to separate deterministic physical behavior from the probability laws governing uncertain inputs. While classical spectral approaches achieve this separation in linear settings, nonlinear responses introduce interactions beyond conventional second-order variability response functions (VRF). Inspired by the spirit of VRFs, this work establishes that, for a fixed physical system, uncertainty propagation is described by a law-invariant operator mapping input realizations to responses, governed by the underlying physics and the deterministic parameters of the system. Different probability laws affect the input sampling and resulting response statistics, but not the mapping operator. We establish this law invariance under complete, invertible coordinate transformations and develop complementary, Fourier, fixed-reference polynomial-chaos (PCE) and finite element method (FEM) transfer formulations. Fourier captures nonlinear cross-frequency interactions and recovers the classical VRF in the appropriate linear limit, PCE describes coupling among stochastic modes, while FEM expresses the deterministic inverse-stiffness action. Neural approximations of these deterministic operators are investigated through analytical and finite-element benchmarks, examining cross-law generalization, the influence of training distributions and stochastic excitation, and the prediction of response fields and statistics. The results demonstrate the potential for reusing learned physical operators across different stochastic laws without retraining, while highlighting the importance of adequate training coverage and the challenges of accurately estimating low-probability events.

papers.title: Consistent Mapping for Fluid Structure Interaction with Geometrically Nonlinear Isogeometric Beams
papers.abstract: Isogeometric beam formulations provide an efficient reduced-dimensional representation of slender structures, combining accurate geometry and high-order continuity with few structural degrees of freedom. Their application to fluid--structure interaction (FSI) requires transferring motion and loads between the one-dimensional beam centerline and the surrounding fluid interface. While mapping strategies exist for conventional finite element beams, geometrically nonlinear isogeometric formulations require operators consistent with their spline-based kinematics and distinct descriptions of cross-sectional rotation. This work develops consistent beam-to-surface mappings for geometrically nonlinear isogeometric Bernoulli and Timoshenko beams in partitioned FSI. Fluid-interface points are attached to the beam in the reference configuration and reconstructed using the nonlinear kinematics of each formulation. Consistent linearization yields a configuration-dependent mapping operator whose transpose ensures work-conjugate load transfer. The formulations are verified through analytical deformation tests, convergence studies, and virtual-work checks, and evaluated in beam-based adaptations of the Mok and Turek--Hron benchmarks and the Goland wing flutter benchmark. The results confirm accurate interface reconstruction and work-conjugate load transfer under large deformations, while demonstrating the applicability of both beam formulations to coupled FSI problems.

papers.title: Calibrating Scientific Foundation Models with Inference-Time Stochastic Attention
papers.abstract: Transformer-based scientific foundation models are increasingly deployed in high-stakes settings, but current architectures give deterministic outputs and provide limited support for calibrated predictive uncertainty. We propose Stochastic Attention, a lightweight sample-average inference-time modification that randomizes attention by replacing softmax weights with normalized multinomial samples controlled by a single concentration parameter, and produces predictive ensembles without retraining. To set this parameter, we introduce a calibration objective that matches the stochastic attention output with the target, yielding an efficient univariate post-hoc tuning problem. We evaluate this mechanism on scientific foundation models for weather and time-series forecasting, as well as a regression task. Across benchmarks against baseline methods, Stochastic Attention achieves the strongest native calibration and the sharpest prediction intervals at comparable calibration, with adaptation costs nearly three orders of magnitude lower than the next-best baseline. Code is available at https://github.com/UQUH/StochasticAttention.

papers.title: Automating structural reliability analysis with a multi-agent large language model framework
papers.abstract: Structural reliability analysis supports the design and safety assessment of buildings and civil infrastructure but requires specialized expertise throughout the workflow. This study presents a multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework that automates component-level reliability analysis from a natural-language problem statement to interpreted estimates of the reliability index and failure probability. Specialized agents handle problem formulation, method planning, code generation, execution, and result interpretation, with human confirmation at key decision points. Numerical reliability estimates are not generated by an LLM; instead, they are obtained solely through deterministic execution of validated solvers. This design mitigates the risk of hallucinated numerical outputs and supports reproducibility. The Method Planner is fine-tuned using quantized low-rank adaptation (QLoRA) for a priori reliability-method category selection. The framework uses open-weight models and supports local execution without closed APIs. Results show that it lowers the expertise barrier to structural reliability assessment while preserving computational trustworthiness.

papers.title: Rethinking Requirement-to-Code Traceability Through Single-Agent and Multi-Agent Approaches
papers.abstract: Requirements-to-code traceability supports essential software engineering activities, including change impact analysis, maintenance, and regulatory compliance. Existing approaches typically rely on a retrieval-and-classification pipeline, which suffers from an inherent retrieval bottleneck: relevant source files that are not retrieved cannot be recovered during subsequent analysis. In this paper, we revisit requirements-to-code traceability in light of the substantially larger context windows offered by modern large language models, which make repository-scale analysis feasible without a separate retrieval step. We propose three approaches: a single-agent approach that analyzes the entire code repository in one pass, and two multi-agent approaches based on self-verification and multi-agent debate. Our evaluation shows that the single-agent approach substantially improves recall, achieving 80.9%, a gain of 38.6 percentage points (pp) over the state-of-the-art retrieval-based baseline, albeit with a 25.8 pp reduction in precision. By leveraging collaborative reasoning, the multi-agent debate-based approach achieves the best overall precision-recall balance, with 24.5% precision and 71.0% recall, yielding an F2 score of 49.5%. This represents an improvement of 7.5 pp over the state of the art and 2.7 pp over the single-agent approach. While the quantitative evaluation establishes the overall effectiveness of the approaches, the aggregate metrics alone explain little due to the considerable variability across results. Importantly, qualitative analysis provides key insights into highly variable quantitative results: the retrieval approach suits requirements that echo the code's vocabulary; single-agent, full-context reasoning suits well-documented, consistently named code; and multi-agent debate suits indirect, conflicting, or distributed evidence.

papers.title: Semi-analytical model for the calculation of solar radiation pressure and its effects on a LEO satellite with predicting the change in position vectors using machine learning techniques
papers.abstract: The rapid increase in the deployment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, catering to diverse applications such as communication, Earth observation, environmental monitoring, and scientific research, has significantly amplified the complexity of trajectory management. The current work focuses on calculating and analyzing perturbation effects on a satellite's anticipated trajectory in LEO, considering Solar Radiation Pressure (SRP) as the main perturbing force. The acceleration due to SRP and it's effects on the satellite was calculated using a custom-built Python module mainly based on the hypothesis of the cannonball model. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed model through comprehensive simulations and comparisons with existing analytical and numerical methods. Here, the primary Keplerian orbital characteristics were employed to analyze a simulated low-earth orbit LEO satellite, initially visualizing the satellite's trajectory and ground tracks at a designated altitude. The study also focuses on a comparative analysis of ground stations, primarily considering the main regions of the subcontinent, with revisit time as the key parameter for comparison. In the end, we combine analytical techniques with Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to predict changes in the position vectors of the satellite. Using ML techniques, the model can adaptively learn and refine predictions based on historical data and real-time input, thus improving accuracy over time. In addition, the incorporation of analytical methods allows for a deeper understanding of the underlying physics governing satellite motion, enabling more precise adjustments and corrections.

papers.title: Wearable-informed generative digital avatars predict task-conditioned post-stroke locomotion
papers.abstract: Dynamic prediction of locomotor capacity after stroke could enable more individualized rehabilitation, yet current assessments largely provide static impairment scores and do not indicate whether patients can perform specific tasks such as slope walking or stair climbing. Here, we present a wearable-informed data-physics hybrid generative framework that reconstructs a stroke survivor's locomotor control from wearable inertial sensing and predicts task-conditioned post-stroke locomotion in new environments. From a single 20 m level-ground walking trial recorded by five IMUs, the framework personalizes a physics-based digital avatar using a healthy-motion prior and hybrid imitation learning, generating dynamically feasible, patient-specific movements for inclined walking and stair negotiation. Across 11 stroke inpatients, predicted postures achieved approximately 95% of the practically attainable accuracy for slope ascent and 80% for stair climbing, respectively, demonstrating reliable task-specific gait prediction. In a multicenter randomized pilot feasibility study (n = 21; 28 days), access to scenario-specific locomotion predictions to support task selection and difficulty titration was associated with larger gains in Fugl-Meyer lower-extremity scores than the control group (mean change 6.0 vs 3.7 points; p < 0.05). These results suggest that wearable-informed generative digital avatars may augment individualized gait rehabilitation planning and provide a pathway toward dynamically personalized post-stroke motor recovery strategies.

papers.title: Partition-of-Unity Gaussian Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
papers.abstract: Gaussian basis functions provide an efficient and flexible alternative to spline activations in Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs), but their performance is sensitive to the Gaussian scale parameter \epsilon. We introduce the partition-of-unity Gaussian KAN (PU-GKAN), a kernel-based normalization framework that transfers the Shepard partition-of-unity principle to trainable KAN edge functions. Each Gaussian edge basis is normalized by its local sum over fixed centers, preserving the standard edge-based architecture and essentially the same trainable coefficient structure as GKAN. The resulting feature map reproduces constants exactly at the edge level and admits an explicit normalized finite-feature kernel interpretation. Numerical experiments show that PU-GKAN reduces sensitivity to \epsilon, improves validation accuracy for most smooth and moderately non-smooth targets, and provides more stable training behavior. These benefits persist across variations in sample size and number of centers, higher-dimensional architectures, and Matern RBF bases. PU-GKAN also improves physics-informed neural networks for Helmholtz and wave equations, with validation-error reductions of up to 90%. These results establish partition-of-unity normalization as a mathematically grounded and broadly applicable framework for improving the reliability and accuracy of radial basis function KANs.

papers.title: VASTO: Simultaneous reconstruction of vascular geometry and blood flow from tomographic projections via differentiable topology optimization
papers.abstract: Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) is widely used to reconstruct vascular geometry from projection measurements, with conventional approaches such as Filtered Back-Projection (FBP) and Iterative Reconstruction (IR) forming the clinical standard. Despite recent advances, these methods remain susceptible to sparse and noisy measurement, making accurate recovery of critical anatomical features challenging. This consequently leads to poor estimation of blood flow. In this work, we present a fluid-physics-constrained reconstruction framework that leverages topology optimization (TO) to jointly recover vascular geometry and blood flow directly from time-resolved CTA sinograms. The formulation couples a steady incompressible flow model with a transient advection-diffusion contrast transport model, mapped to sinogram space through a differentiable projection operator. The velocity field is recovered as part of the reconstruction, and thus hemodynamic information can be obtained without requiring a separate computational fluid dynamics pipeline. The proposed method is demonstrated on synthetic phantoms under varying sparsity and noise levels, and on representative projection data.

papers.title: State space modeling of RLC ladder circuits
papers.abstract: Large-scale electrical circuits span a wide range of research topics from highly integrated circuits in microelectronics up to power grids for cities and countries. As the complexity increases significantly by each additional component, we find a need to describe large-scale circuits in a manner easy to understand. In this article, we study cascades of simple circuits consisting of resistors, capacitors and inductors, which we call ladder circuits. Such electrical ladders are common in electronics to design filters and they are also used in other disciplines, for example to describe diffusion or wave phenomena. In particular, we derive linear time-invariant state space models for three simple ladder types and we discuss the specific matrix structures of the large-scale second-order differential equations. Furthermore, we exemplify our findings with simulations to unveil the intrinsic dynamical behavior of each ladder type.

papers.title: Decompose Dynamics Before Learning Dependencies in Spatiotemporal Systems
papers.abstract: Relations in networked spatiotemporal systems are often learned from observations that entangle dynamics governed by different mechanisms, obscuring what evolves locally and how it propagates across nodes. We introduce Component-Aware Network Dynamics with Ordered Relations (CANDOR), which decomposes local dynamics before learning their dependencies. CANDOR represents each trajectory through a persistent background, gradual accumulation and release, and sparse shocks. Conditioned on these components, a delay-aware physical branch models edge and sample-dependent propagation over directed topology, while a topology-unconstrained functional branch discovers latent dependencies from background dynamics. Context-adaptive fusion combines functional, forward-propagation, and reverse-support forecasts, with training objectives encouraging specialized and semantically consistent representations. Experiments on two traffic benchmarks and three long-horizon water-quality datasets span two distinct spatiotemporal systems: human-driven urban traffic and naturally evolving river water quality. CANDOR achieves the lowest aggregate normalized error across five datasets, outperforming the overall runner-up by 7.25%. These results establish decomposition before dependency learning as an effective principle for spatiotemporal representation learning.

papers.title: From language-model stock rankings to testable economic rules: A computational audit
papers.abstract: We test the stability, reproducibility and investment outcomes of language-model stock rankings. Four models and five numerical comparators share a portfolio engine over 72 monthly holding periods in the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) 50, China Securities Index (CSI) 300 and CSI 500. Rankings use nine characteristics, and five repeated SSE 50 runs measure variation under identical inputs. Linear rules fitted to development-period model preferences are frozen before unseen-month, larger-pool and controlled-intervention tests. Their mean Spearman agreement with model rankings is 0.923-0.984 in the SSE 50 and 0.795-0.985 after transfer. Aggregate rank-change error falls relative to a zero-change prediction in twelve archived feature-group comparisons and eight matched single-feature comparisons, with Holm adjustments applied in separate nine-plus-three and six-plus-two families. Prediction of individual entries and exits remains weak (event Jaccard 0.000-0.125). Historical mean model compound annual growth rates range from 6.26% to 11.17%. At 10 basis points per side and six-month blocks, the twelve-comparison model-minus-rule return family and factor-controlled associations yield no adjusted finding. Three higher-cost, twelve-month-block comparisons favor a Terra rule within their twelve-test slices, with no adjusted finding across the full 144-test sensitivity grid. Two input-intervention batches totaling 5,184 responses supply paired intervention-return tests. The three-model batch has no bootstrap-adjusted finding at the primary block length; a Luna row-order effect appears under heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent (HAC) adjustment within its three-test family but not in a pooled 24-test adjustment. Compact rules approximate aggregate rankings; return conclusions depend on comparison families, uncertainty methods and tie priorities.

papers.title: MindVLM: Neural-Grounded Visual Captioning via Subject-Aware Semantic Evidence Selection
papers.abstract: Translating visual brain activity into natural language offers a powerful window into human cognition and neural semantic representation. Most prior brain-captioning approaches project fMRI signals into language space using paired supervision. However, the widely used Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD) was built based only on image-fMRI pairs, while existing methods rely on MS-COCO captions as indirect textual supervision. Critically, during fMRI acquisition, participants observe only cropped image regions, whereas the associated MS-COCO captions describe full scenes. This mismatch creates a fundamental gap between neural representations and textual supervision, introducing an inherent semantic loss in NSD-based brain captioning. To mitigate this limitation, we reformulate brain captioning as Neural-Grounded Visual Captioning, where language is generated directly from visually grounded neural evidence rather than text supervision. We propose MindVLM, a framework that maps fMRI signals into subject-aware visual tokens and leverages a frozen vision-language model (VLM) to produce interpretable and personalized descriptions. Instead of point-wise regression, MindVLM focuses on extracting semantically relevant visual cues from neural activity, naturally accommodating partial observability and inter-subject variability. Extensive experiments on NSD show that MindVLM maintains, and often improves, caption quality across multiple VLM backbones, including LLaVA-v1.5, Qwen2.5-VL, and Gemma3, beyond intrinsic model priors. Despite requiring neither text supervision nor an LLM during training and operating under an image-grounded inference paradigm distinct from conventional captioning methods, MindVLM remains competitive with supervised approaches, suggesting that subject-specific neural grounding provides an efficient, scalable, and interpretable path toward faithful brain-to-language generation.

papers.title: Transverse impulse response of finite and infinite Rayleigh beams
papers.abstract: Here, we study an undamped Rayleigh beam subjected to a concentrated transverse impulse applied at a point far from the boundaries. For a simply supported finite beam struck at its midpoint, using the modal expansion of the impulse response, a short-time asymptotic series for the response of the struck point is derived. The infinite beam impulse response is obtained as a spectral integral in two ways. The spectral integral is evaluated exactly in terms of modified Bessel functions via Laplace transform calculations. The corresponding short- and long-time asymptotics of the exact integral are consistent with the power series developed earlier and the Euler-Bernoulli beam, respectively. Direct numerical evaluation of the integral with a pre-specified error bound and numerical contour integration is also presented for verification. An ad hoc approximation is given which matches the response well for all times. The relationship between finite and infinite beam responses is examined in some detail. There are three consequences of finite length. First, the coefficients in the power series expansion contain components that decay exponentially with increasing length of the beam. Second, a smooth deviation from the infinite beam response is observed, consistent with the greatest group velocity in the beam, wherein a small precursor is detected which is consistent with broader theory. Third, a slope discontinuity is observed, corresponding to the high-frequency limit of group velocity. The full time series plot from modal expansion satisfactorily shows both the arrival and passage of these high frequency components. This paper opens the door to impact studies that are envisaged in future work.
